tei:titleStmt.tei:title: Prayer of the Guest Chaplain of the U.S. House of Representatives: Rabbi Selig S. Auerbach on 20 July 1955

tei:div.tei:head: Prayer of the Guest Chaplain of the U.S. House of Representatives: Rabbi Selig S. Auerbach on 20 July 1955

tei:lg.tei:l: at the beginning of this session
we again turn to Thee for guidance.
with the Representatives of our Nation.
for the true benefit of this great country of ours,
and to the betterment of the entire world.
for the purpose of restoring true peace
realize the truth of the words spoken by Thy prophet
that two opponents can walk together
only if both parties commit themselves
to adhere to their agreements in truth,
Let the time not be distant
when the words of Thy great seer will be fulfilled
that the lamb will rest next to the wolf,
Then the time will be here
when the world can be arranged
the vision shared by Thy prophets
and the Founding Fathers of our Republic.
we ask for Thy blessing, O God,

tei:note.tei:p: This was the Geneva Summit (1955), a Cold War-era meeting in Geneva, Switzerland. Held on July 18, 1955, it was a meeting of “The Big Four”: President Dwight D. Eisenhower of the United States, Prime Minister Anthony Eden of Britain, Premier Nikolai A. Bulganin of the Soviet Union, and Prime Minister Edgar Faure of France. The first such meeting since the Potsdam Conference ten years earlier, the purpose of the Summit was to bring together world leaders to begin discussions on peace. Although those discussions led down many different roads (arms negotiations, trade barriers, diplomacy, nuclear warfare, etc.), the talks were influenced by the common goal for increased global security.

The employ of the translation “Prince of Peace” based on שַׂר־שָׁלֽוֹם from Isaiah 9:5 is remarkable in a Jewish prayer, since this usage is widely understood by trinitarian Christians to refer to their messianic deity. Possibly it is here offered as an extraordinary ecumenical gesture. If anyone can help to explain this further, please leave a comment or contact us. –Aharon Varady
